You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure, and several recent issue reports that have been pre-filtered by an external semantic retrieval model (SBERT) to be the most relevant to this failure among recent reports.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– likely-relevant recent bug reports,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The failing test expects a NotPositiveDefiniteMatrixException to be thrown when instantiating CholeskyDecompositionImpl with a matrix containing negative off-diagonal elements. The constructor of CholeskyDecompositionImpl called by the test (lines 93-151) performs initial checks on the matrix:

- First, it verifies the matrix is square.
- Then it retrieves the internal data array lTData.
- It iterates through the matrix checking diagonal elements are above an absolute positivity threshold - if any are below, it throws NotPositiveDefiniteMatrixException.
- For off-diagonal elements above the diagonal (j > i), it checks symmetry within a relative symmetry threshold, throwing NotSymmetricMatrixException otherwise. Importantly, it sets the lower triangle below the diagonal elements (lJ[i]) to zero explicitly.
- After checks, it transforms the matrix into the Cholesky decomposition by processing rows, taking square roots of diagonal elements and updating the lower triangle accordingly.

The current bug report states that the test matrix with negative off-diagonal elements does not throw NotPositiveDefiniteMatrixException, although the test expects it. Inspecting the constructor shows that the diagonal elements alone are checked against positivity threshold for raising NotPositiveDefiniteMatrixException (line 114). Off-diagonal elements, including negatives, are not checked for positivity but only for symmetry (line 124). No exception is thrown just because off-diagonal elements are negative.

This behavior aligns with the mathematical definition: a positive definite matrix must have positive pivots/diagonal elements, but off-diagonal values can be negative as long as the matrix is symmetric positive definite. The test expects an exception due to negative off-diagonal values, but the actual implementation only regards positive diagonal values as a criterion for not being positive definite.

Hence the cause of failure is the test wrongly assuming that negative off-diagonal matrix elements cause a NotPositiveDefiniteMatrixException, when in reality the implementation treats the matrix as valid if the diagonal is positive and the matrix is symmetric within the threshold.

In summary, the bug is a mismatch between the test's expectation and the mathematical condition applied in CholeskyDecompositionImpl. The constructor's implementation only throws NotPositiveDefiniteMatrixException when the diagonal elements fail the positivity test, not for negative off-diagonal elements.

Recent bug reports do not mention related issues about this matrix or these checks and are unrelated.

The issue is not an error in the implementation but an incorrect test assumption about when NotPositiveDefiniteMatrixException is thrown.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
